title: Six Hundred More Years
prompt: A heritage project's restoration film, and the hardest input case so far: a commentary that must be read as written (dates, quarry, the 1612 / 1875 / 2019 floods, a 6:1 hot-mixed lime, nineteen months — not a figure may change), three real photographs the bridge on screen has to match, the craftsman's own recorded English narration to be used as his voice rather than re-dubbed, and a string bed underneath. The bridge is locked to the uploaded photos through an identity anchor built FROM them, so the single segmental arch, the grey limestone and the wide pale mortar joints hold across all nine shots. Subtitles are transcribed from the craftsman's recording; the ASR mishears the French place names, so two proper nouns are spelled differently from the script.
